name: Small Bowel Atresia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Small Bowel Atresia

criteria.description: Neonatal intestinal obstruction presenting with bilious vomiting and abdominal distension
Abdominal X-ray showing multiple dilated bowel loops with absence of distal gas
Contrast enema demonstrating microcolon or absence of distal bowel filling
Intraoperative identification of atretic segment of small intestine

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation with radiologic findings or surgical confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Prenatal ultrasound may show polyhydramnios and dilated bowel loops but is not diagnostic.

imaging: Abdominal X-ray showing multiple dilated proximal bowel loops with air-fluid levels
Contrast enema showing microcolon or absence of distal bowel filling
Prenatal ultrasound showing polyhydramnios and dilated bowel loops
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic occurrence
Rare associations with chromosomal abnormalities (e.g., trisomy 21)
other: Intraoperative confirmation of atretic bowel segment
Histopathology showing absence or discontinuity of bowel lumen

distinguishingFeatures: Delayed passage of meconium beyond 48 hours
Absence of ganglion cells on rectal biopsy
Characteristic soap-bubble or ground-glass appearance on abdominal X-ray
Contrast enema shows microcolon with inspissated meconium

redFlags: Failure to pass meconium within 48 hours
Progressive abdominal distension with signs of sepsis
references: Moore SW, et al. Small bowel atresia: a review of 50 cases. Pediatr Surg Int. 2019.
Orphanet: Small bowel atresia. Orphanet Report Series. 2021.
Kliegman RM, et al. Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics, 21st Edition. 2020.
